title: The Great Gatsby
author: F. Scott Fitzgerald
modernization_rationale: 1925 American prose, largely transparent to modern readers; period references (bond business, Prohibition, specific 1920s celebrities/brands) occasionally need light contextual handling but Fitzgerald's syntax and diction remain accessible.

segments.title: I

signatures.passage_hint: In my younger and more vulnerable years my father gave me some advice that I've been turning over in my mind ever since.
signatures.why: The novel's famous opening sentence; establishes Nick's retrospective voice.

signatures.passage_hint: Whenever you feel like criticizing anyone, just remember that all the people in this world haven't had the advantages that you've had.
signatures.why: One of the most quoted lines in American fiction; sets Nick's claim to reserved judgment.

signatures.passage_hint: Reserving judgements is a matter of infinite hope. I am still a little afraid of missing something if I forget that, as my father snobbishly suggested, and I snobbishly repeat, a sense of the fundamental decencies is parcelled out unequally at birth.
signatures.why: Voice-establishing; the key to Nick's unreliability.

signatures.passage_hint: If personality is an unbroken series of successful gestures, then there was something gorgeous about him, some heightened sensitivity to the promises of life
signatures.why: Novel's thesis statement about Gatsby.

signatures.passage_hint: it was an extraordinary gift for hope, a romantic readiness such as I have never found in any other person and which it is not likely I shall ever find again.
signatures.why: 'Romantic readiness' is critically load-bearing.

signatures.passage_hint: The only completely stationary object in the room was an enormous couch on which two young women were buoyed up as though upon an anchored balloon.
signatures.why: Signature set-piece prose establishing Daisy and Jordan as ethereal.

signatures.passage_hint: I hope she'll be a fool—that's the best thing a girl can be in this world, a beautiful little fool.
signatures.why: Central to feminist readings of Daisy; universally quoted.

signatures.passage_hint: he stretched out his arms toward the dark water in a curious way, and, far as I was from him, I could have sworn he was trembling.
signatures.why: First appearance of the green light — novel's central symbol.

signatures.passage_hint: Sophisticated—God, I'm sophisticated!
signatures.why: Captures Daisy's performed cynicism; pivot of Nick's reading of her insincerity.

signatures.passage_hint: distinguished nothing except a single green light, minute and far away, that might have been the end of a dock.
signatures.why: The green light as material object — closes the chapter's mythic opening.

segments.notes: Highest-priority preservation chapter: establishes narrator voice, Tom/Daisy/Jordan, West Egg geography, and the green light. Compress the family-background and bond-business paragraphs aggressively; preserve the dinner scene's tonal texture and Daisy's voice. Keep Tom's racist 'Nordic' outburst in compressed form — it characterizes him and reverberates later.

segments.title: II

signatures.passage_hint: This is a valley of ashes—a fantastic farm where ashes grow like wheat into ridges and hills and grotesque gardens
signatures.why: Signature set-piece and major symbol.

signatures.passage_hint: the eyes of Doctor T. J. Eckleburg. The eyes of Doctor T. J. Eckleburg are blue and gigantic—their retinas are one yard high.
signatures.why: Iconic image; later weaponized as 'God sees everything.'

signatures.passage_hint: With the influence of the dress her personality had also undergone a change. The intense vitality that had been so remarkable in the garage was converted into impressive hauteur.
signatures.why: Nick's ironic observation of Myrtle's class-performance.

signatures.passage_hint: Making a short deft movement, Tom Buchanan broke her nose with his open hand.
signatures.why: The chapter's shocking pivot; must be preserved for character and tone.

signatures.passage_hint: I was within and without, simultaneously enchanted and repelled by the inexhaustible variety of life.
signatures.why: Nick's signature self-definition — key to every reading of the narrator's doubleness.

signatures.passage_hint: Beauty and the Beast … Loneliness … Old Grocery Horse … Brook'n Bridge …
signatures.why: The fragmentary ellipsis ending — signature prosodic device.

segments.notes: Dense with period apparatus (Town Tattle, Simon Called Peter, McKees). Compress the McKee/Catherine gossip heavily; preserve the valley of ashes opening, Eckleburg, the apartment's transformation of Myrtle, and the broken-nose moment. Retain Nick's 'within and without' aside verbatim.

segments.title: III

signatures.passage_hint: In his blue gardens men and girls came and went like moths among the whisperings and the champagne and the stars.
signatures.why: Iconic signature sentence.

signatures.passage_hint: Every Friday five crates of oranges and lemons arrived from a fruiterer in New York—every Monday these same oranges and lemons left his back door in a pyramid of pulpless halves.
signatures.why: Signature catalogue-of-excess voice.

signatures.passage_hint: He smiled understandingly—much more than understandingly. It was one of those rare smiles with a quality of eternal reassurance in it, that you may come across four or five times in life.
signatures.why: The famous 'Gatsby's smile' paragraph.

signatures.passage_hint: Precisely at that point it vanished—and I was looking at an elegant young roughneck, a year or two over thirty, whose elaborate formality of speech just missed being absurd.
signatures.why: First crack in Gatsby's performance — critically foregrounded.

signatures.passage_hint: Absolutely real—have pages and everything. I thought they'd be a nice durable cardboard.
signatures.why: Owl Eyes in the library — comic touchstone that will echo at the funeral.

signatures.passage_hint: The lights grow brighter as the earth lurches away from the sun, and now the orchestra is playing yellow cocktail music, and the opera of voices pitches a key higher.
signatures.why: Signature party-prose; register-defining.

signatures.passage_hint: Everyone suspects himself of at least one of the cardinal virtues, and this is mine: I am one of the few honest people that I have ever known.
signatures.why: Famous closing line — pivot of unreliable-narrator reading.

signatures.passage_hint: At the enchanted metropolitan twilight I felt a haunting loneliness sometimes, and felt it in others—poor young clerks who loitered in front of windows
signatures.why: Voice-establishing lyrical digression on New York.

signatures.passage_hint: She wasn't able to endure being at a disadvantage and, given this unwillingness, I suppose she had begun dealing in subterfuges when she was very young
signatures.why: Nick's characterization of Jordan — sets up the 'careless people' theme.

segments.notes: Longest non-VII chapter and densely signature-rich. Compress the crowd-texture catalogues but preserve at least one signature run; retain Gatsby's introduction and smile fully; preserve Owl Eyes episode as it recurs at the funeral. Preserve Nick's New York lyrical aside and the closing honest-people line.

segments.title: IV

signatures.passage_hint: From East Egg, then, came the Chester Beckers and the Leeches, and a man named Bunsen, whom I knew at Yale, and Doctor Webster Civet, who was drowned last summer up in Maine.
signatures.why: Signature mock-Homeric catalogue — central to the book's satirical texture.

signatures.passage_hint: I am the son of some wealthy people in the Middle West—all dead now. I was brought up in America but educated at Oxford
signatures.why: Gatsby's self-invented biography — load-bearing for later unmasking.

signatures.passage_hint: The city seen from the Queensboro Bridge is always the city seen for the first time, in its first wild promise of all the mystery and the beauty in the world.
signatures.why: Signature lyrical aside on New York.

signatures.passage_hint: Anything can happen now that we've slid over this bridge, I thought; anything at all … Even Gatsby could happen, without any particular wonder.
signatures.why: Famous coda to the bridge passage.

signatures.passage_hint: A small, flat-nosed Jew raised his large head and regarded me with two fine growths of hair which luxuriated in either nostril.
signatures.why: Signature grotesque-comic description; critically engaged for Fitzgerald's caricature style.

signatures.passage_hint: He's the man who fixed the World's Series back in 1919.
signatures.why: Structural plot pivot — Wolfshiem as underworld context for Gatsby.

signatures.passage_hint: Gatsby bought that house so that Daisy would be just across the bay.
signatures.why: The structural pivot of the novel — the revelation that reframes everything.

signatures.passage_hint: He had waited five years and bought a mansion where he dispensed starlight to casual moths—so that he could 'come over' some afternoon to a stranger's garden.
signatures.why: Nick's framing of Gatsby's quest as absurd/sublime.

signatures.passage_hint: There are only the pursued, the pursuing, the busy, and the tired.
signatures.why: Famous Jordan-quoted phrase; closes the chapter's urban movement.

segments.notes: Chapter has two distinct movements: Gatsby's autobiography + Wolfshiem lunch, and Jordan's Louisville retrospection + the reveal. Compress the guest-list catalogue to one vivid paragraph; preserve Gatsby's biography in compressed form (needed for Ch. VIII contrast); keep the Jordan-narrated Louisville scene lean but intact; the 'bought that house so that Daisy would be just across the bay' reveal must land with force.

segments.title: V

signatures.passage_hint: Gatsby, pale as death, with his hands plunged like weights in his coat pockets, was standing in a puddle of water glaring tragically into my eyes.
signatures.why: Signature comic-pathetic image.

signatures.passage_hint: His head leaned back so far that it rested against the face of a defunct mantelpiece clock
signatures.why: The clock-tilting scene — central comic-tragic image of time/repetition.

signatures.passage_hint: They're such beautiful shirts, she sobbed, her voice muffled in the thick folds. It makes me sad because I've never seen such—such beautiful shirts before.
signatures.why: One of the most discussed passages in the novel; central to readings of Daisy's materialism.

signatures.passage_hint: His count of enchanted objects had diminished by one.
signatures.why: The moment the green light loses its symbolic charge — critically load-bearing.

signatures.passage_hint: No amount of fire or freshness can challenge what a man can store up in his ghostly heart.
signatures.why: Summation of Gatsby's dream-beyond-object.

signatures.passage_hint: There must have been moments even that afternoon when Daisy tumbled short of his dreams—not through her own fault, but because of the colossal vitality of his illusion.
signatures.why: 'Colossal vitality of his illusion' — one of the most-quoted critical phrases.

signatures.passage_hint: The rich get richer and the poor get—children.
signatures.why: Klipspringer's song as ironic comment on the scene.

segments.notes: The reunion chapter — every beat matters. Compress the rain-and-mower setup efficiently; preserve the mantelpiece-clock scene, the shirts scene, the green-light reassessment, and the closing meditation on Gatsby's dream exceeding its object. Keep Klipspringer brief but in.

segments.title: VI

signatures.passage_hint: The truth was that Jay Gatsby of West Egg, Long Island, sprang from his Platonic conception of himself. He was a son of God
signatures.why: Among the most-cited sentences in American literary criticism.

signatures.passage_hint: I suppose he'd had the name ready for a long time, even then. His parents were shiftless and unsuccessful farm people—his imagination had never really accepted them as his parents at all.
signatures.why: Critically important for readings of self-invention.

signatures.passage_hint: he must be about His Father's business, the service of a vast, vulgar, and meretricious beauty.
signatures.why: Key theological-aesthetic formulation for Gatsby's mission.

signatures.passage_hint: It was James Gatz who had been loafing along the beach that afternoon in a torn green jersey and a pair of canvas pants, but it was already Jay Gatsby who borrowed a rowboat
signatures.why: The moment of self-invention — structurally pivotal.

signatures.passage_hint: Can't repeat the past? he cried incredulously. Why of course you can!
signatures.why: Iconic Gatsby line — thesis of his tragedy.

signatures.passage_hint: His heart beat faster as Daisy's white face came up to his own. He knew that when he kissed this girl, and forever wed his unutterable visions to her perishable breath, his mind would never romp again like the mind of God.
signatures.why: Canonical lyrical set-piece in Fitzgerald criticism.

signatures.passage_hint: She was appalled by West Egg, this unprecedented 'place' that Broadway had begotten upon a Long Island fishing village
signatures.why: Daisy's class-recoil — load-bearing for the novel's social architecture.

segments.notes: Chapter is half backstory (Dan Cody, Gatz→Gatsby) and half the awkward Tom-at-the-party evening. Compress the Cody section but preserve the 'Platonic conception' passage and the naming moment. Compress the party-through-Daisy's-eyes but preserve the 'She was appalled by West Egg' framing. End with the kiss flashback intact — it's one of the novel's great lyrical moments.

segments.title: VII

signatures.passage_hint: Her voice is full of money, he said suddenly.
signatures.why: Among the most-quoted lines in American fiction — hinge of economic readings of Daisy.

signatures.passage_hint: That was it. I'd never understood before. It was full of money—that was the inexhaustible charm that rose and fell in it, the jingle of it, the cymbals' song of it … High in a white palace the king's daughter, the golden girl
signatures.why: The 'golden girl' coda — novel's most condensed statement of its economic-romantic theme.

signatures.passage_hint: Bles-sed pre-cious
signatures.why: Pammy's entrance — the child Gatsby never believed in.

signatures.passage_hint: You resemble the advertisement of the man
signatures.why: Daisy's declaration in front of Tom — the moment the secret becomes visible.

signatures.passage_hint: I suppose the latest thing is to sit back and let Mr. Nobody from Nowhere make love to your wife.
signatures.why: Tom's class-fury — the confrontation's ideological core.

signatures.passage_hint: Your wife doesn't love you, said Gatsby. She's never loved you. She loves me.
signatures.why: The plaza confrontation's pivot.

signatures.passage_hint: Oh, you want too much! she cried to Gatsby. I love you now—isn't that enough? I can't help what's past.
signatures.why: Daisy's collapse — the dream's impossibility made explicit.

signatures.passage_hint: only the dead dream fought on as the afternoon slipped away, trying to touch what was no longer tangible
signatures.why: Key image of the failed quest.

signatures.passage_hint: Thirty—the promise of a decade of loneliness, a thinning list of single men to know, a thinning briefcase of enthusiasm, thinning hair.
signatures.why: Nick's signature anaphoric melancholy.

signatures.passage_hint: So we drove on toward death through the cooling twilight.
signatures.why: Signature closing sentence of the movement — prosodically unmistakable.

signatures.passage_hint: Myrtle Wilson, her life violently extinguished, knelt in the road and mingled her thick dark blood with the dust.
signatures.why: The killing — novel's narrative hinge.

signatures.passage_hint: her eyes, wide with jealous terror, were fixed not on Tom, but on Jordan Baker, whom she took to be his wife.
signatures.why: Myrtle's fatal misrecognition — plot-critical.

signatures.passage_hint: They weren't happy, and neither of them had touched the chicken or the ale—and yet they weren't unhappy either. There was an unmistakable air of natural intimacy about the picture
signatures.why: The conspiracy scene through the pantry window — 'careless people' set up.

segments.notes: Longest chapter and structurally the climax: luncheon, Plaza confrontation, accident, aftermath. This is where compression pressure is greatest — preserve the full Plaza confrontation arc (voice-of-money revelation → 'Mr. Nobody from Nowhere' → Daisy's collapse), Myrtle's death, and the pantry-window tableau. Compress the opening heat-of-the-train and Biloxi anecdote, and lean on 'So we drove on toward death' as the movement's closing beat. The Michaelis inquest-testimony framing can be tightened.

segments.title: VIII

signatures.passage_hint: She was the first 'nice' girl he had ever known.
signatures.why: Opens the Daisy-Louisville flashback — key to Gatsby's class-wound.

signatures.passage_hint: He felt married to her, that was all.
signatures.why: Summation of Gatsby's irrevocable commitment.

signatures.passage_hint: of the freshness of many clothes, and of Daisy, gleaming like silver, safe and proud above the hot struggles of the poor.
signatures.why: Signature image of Daisy as preserved by wealth.

signatures.passage_hint: They're a rotten crowd, I shouted across the lawn. You're worth the whole damn bunch put together.
signatures.why: One of the novel's most quoted lines — Nick's moral judgment crystallized.

signatures.passage_hint: He must have felt that he had lost the old warm world, paid a high price for living too long with a single dream.
signatures.why: 'Old warm world' — quoted in virtually every scholarly treatment of Gatsby's death.

signatures.passage_hint: A new world, material without being real, where poor ghosts, breathing dreams like air, drifted fortuitously about … like that ashen, fantastic figure gliding toward him through the amorphous trees.
signatures.why: The death's lyrical summation; Wilson as ashen figure completes the valley-of-ashes motif.

signatures.passage_hint: the holocaust was complete.
signatures.why: Signature closing sentence of the chapter — prosodic and thematic weight.

signatures.passage_hint: It was this night that he told me the strange story of his youth with Dan Cody—told it to me because 'Jay Gatsby' had broken up like glass against Tom's hard malice
signatures.why: Nick's framing of the long disclosure; voice-establishing.

segments.notes: The Daisy-Louisville retrospection and the death. Compress the 'Beale Street Blues' Daisy-drifting passage but preserve its lyrical texture; keep 'rotten crowd / worth the whole damn bunch' verbatim; preserve the meditation on the lost warm world and the ashen figure gliding through the trees. The Wilson-Michaelis vigil is already in Ch. VIII's closing — tighten but preserve 'God sees everything' as callback to Eckleburg.

segments.title: IX

signatures.passage_hint: Schedule … Rise from bed 6:00 a.m.
signatures.why: Gatz showing the schedule — one of the novel's most affecting scenes and load-bearing for self-making.

signatures.passage_hint: The poor son-of-a-bitch, he said.
signatures.why: Owl Eyes at the funeral — one of the book's most famous closing character beats.

signatures.passage_hint: That's my Middle West—not the wheat or the prairies or the lost Swede towns, but the thrilling returning trains of my youth, and the street lamps and sleigh bells in the frosty dark
signatures.why: Voice-establishing lyrical digression — load-bearing for regionalist readings.

signatures.passage_hint: They were careless people, Tom and Daisy—they smashed up things and creatures and then retreated back into their money or their vast carelessness
signatures.why: Among the most-quoted indictments in American literature.

signatures.passage_hint: a fresh, green breast of the new world. Its vanished trees, the trees that had made way for Gatsby's house, had once pandered in whispers to the last and greatest of all human dreams
signatures.why: Canonical American-dream set-piece.

signatures.passage_hint: face to face for the last time in history with something commensurate to his capacity for wonder.
signatures.why: 'Capacity for wonder' anchors readings of the novel's American-dream thesis.

signatures.passage_hint: Gatsby believed in the green light, the orgiastic future that year by year recedes before us.
signatures.why: Iconic penultimate passage.

signatures.passage_hint: So we beat on, boats against the current, borne back ceaselessly into the past.
signatures.why: The novel's famous closing sentence — the single most-quoted line in the book.

signatures.passage_hint: Blessed are the dead that the rain falls on
signatures.why: Owl Eyes' benediction at the graveside.

signatures.passage_hint: What if I did tell him? That fellow had it coming to him.
signatures.why: Tom's confession — structurally necessary for the 'careless people' judgment.

signatures.passage_hint: Let us learn to show our friendship for a man when he is alive and not after he is dead
signatures.why: Wolfshiem's refusal — key moral beat in the funeral sequence.

segments.notes: The coda. Compress Wolfshiem's office visit and Klipspringer's call efficiently, but preserve both as moral indictments. The schedule, the funeral with Owl Eyes, the Middle West reverie, the careless-people passage, the Dutch-sailors reverie, and the final two paragraphs must all land with full force. This is the chapter where budget should skew toward preservation — the closing pages are essentially all signature.

motifs.name: the green light
motifs.description: Gatsby's signal across the bay; figure for the receding American dream. Begins as concrete dock-light, becomes symbol, then returns to mere object after Daisy's presence diminishes it.
indicative_phrases: green light at the end of Daisy's dock

motifs.name: eyes that watch / Eckleburg
motifs.description: The oculist's billboard over the valley of ashes, later Wilson's 'God sees everything.' Links surveillance, judgment, advertising, and absent deity.
indicative_phrases: eyes of Doctor T. J. Eckleburg

motifs.name: ashes and dust
motifs.description: The valley of ashes as moral and industrial waste — ash-grey men, ash-heaps, the 'foul dust' that 'floated in the wake of his dreams,' and finally the ashen figure of Wilson gliding toward Gatsby.

motifs.name: voice full of money
motifs.description: Daisy's voice as the novel's acoustic signature and its economic emblem.

motifs.name: carelessness
motifs.description: Jordan's driving, Tom and Daisy's social habits, the careless rich 'retreated back into their money.' The novel's central ethical indictment.

motifs.name: hot/cool, light/dark, clothes as value
motifs.description: Summer heat as pressure, cool dresses and interiors as privilege; white dresses, silver, gold. Clothing indexes class and unreality.

plan_notes: Voice-driven first-person: Nick's register IS the book. Preserve his characteristic moves — the balanced hedging sentence, the ironic catalogue, the sudden lyrical digression, and the retrospective framing ('when I came back from the East last autumn'). Do not neutralize his snobbery or his contradictions; they are the point. Two specific cautions: (1) Fitzgerald's ethnic caricatures (Wolfshiem's nose; the 'modish negroes' on Blackwell's Island; Mrs. McKee's 'little kike') are critically engaged period material — preserve in compressed form rather than sanitize, as downstream readers expect them. Don't expand or soften. (2) Chapter VII is where compression pressure concentrates; budget must bias toward preservation of the Plaza confrontation's full arc rather than cutting individual exchanges. The book's famous closing pages (careless people → fresh green breast → capacity for wonder → green light → boats against the current) should be preserved almost fully; borrow budget from chapters II, IV's Wolfshiem lunch, and VI's Cody backstory as needed. Period register: keep 'old sport,' 'bond business,' 'highball,' 'rotogravure' — these date the text productively. The novel's structural irony (Nick claims to reserve judgment, then delivers the most damning judgments in American fiction) must survive compression — preserve both the claim (Ch. I opening) and the verdict (Ch. IX 'careless people').
